en.title: Almost Persuaded
en.author: Philip P. Bliss
stanzas:
"Almost persuaded," harvest is past!
"Almost persuaded," doom comes at last!
"Almost" cannot avail;
"Almost" is but to fail!
Sad, sad, that bitter wail—
"Almost," but lost!

notes: Text from Timeless Truths (The Blue Book #104). Hymnary's representative text (AME Hymnal #275) has the same three stanzas, spelling 'lingering' and 'wanderer' in full where TT elides them to the note, and ending a few lines differently. TT kept. Words and music both Bliss, 1871. Tune: hymnary files it under its first line, '[Almost persuaded now to believe] (Bliss)'; ALMOST PERSUADED is the name most hymnals use. Meter 9.9.6.6.6.4. Key G: hymnary's instances run 25 G to 4 E-flat and 3 F; TT prints G, already a guitar key. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat. The opening bars run I through chromatic augmented passing chords (Eaug, Baug) that are alto motion, not harmony, and were dropped; 'now to believe' is vi-V-I, 'Christ to receive' V-I; 'Seems now some soul to say' IV-I; 'Go, Spirit, go Thy way' V-I with a V7sus4 over the tonic dropped; 'Some more convenient day' I-ii7-IV-I (the I/B between ii7 and IV dropped); the close is a cadential 6/4 into V7, written D7.
